title: Consul Johan Magnus Wenström's despatches from Salé in a 3-digit consular code, deciphered between the lines (probable key to consul Wulff's bare cipher)
correspondents: Johan Magnus Wenström (Swedish consul, later consul general, at Salé and Tangier) -> the Kanslipresident and the Kanslikollegium (Stockholm)
language: Swedish (cipher: 3-digit groups 100-799, comma-separated, in rows between clear lines)
shelfmark: Riksarkivet, Diplomatica Maroccana, SE/RA/2112/II/II - IX (Generalkonsuln Johan Magnus Wenström i Tanger, skrivelser 1775-1787)
folio_note: 281 images (series R0003633), all paged. Cipher at 13 (Salé 6 Nov 1775), 15, 16 (6 Nov 1775), 18 (= 19, second exposure; Salé 20 Feb 1776), 23, 24, 27 (Salé 15 May 1776). No cipher after May 1776.
status: Catalogue: consul's letters, no mention of cipher. Glossed: on 13, 15, 16 (2600 px) the decipherment is written above each digit row (13: `sjö vid flera tillfällen nog orsakt igenom dess djerfhet` over `406658430188...`); on 23, 24, 27 the digit rows are struck through with heavy strokes, the clear text written between. Groups `374,507`, `212,380`, `380` recur here and in consul Wulff's bare Salé string `4471683745073806223843` (lead 2314, 1764-65), which splits as `447 168 374 507 380 622 384`; von Stauden's 1775 reports (lead 2318) use the same layout. Probably one Kanslikollegium consular code for Morocco 1764-76.
why: Glossed pairs from the same consulate a decade after Wulff: if the code is the same, Wenström's letters give the table to read Wulff's bare cipher of 1764-65 (the peace presents for the Sultan) and von Stauden's bare rows of 1775.
verify: Transcribe the glossed rows of 13, 15, 16, 18 into group/plaintext pairs; test the table on Wulff's bare strings (Maroccana II/I images 11-14, 17, 18, 22, 24) and on von Stauden's bare rows (Maroccana I/I images 76, 79); compare with Molinari's glossed Tunis groups (Tunisica 7/2, lead 2260).
prior_art: open as far as checked (6 Nov 2026): known.py finds nothing on the shelfmark or the correspondents; DECODE, Tomokiyo, Lasry and the editions not searched for these letters
source: Riksarkivet consular volumes, full paging (Maroccana, Turcica bihang Algerica/Tunisica/Tripolitana; IIIF, Referer route), Nov 2026

title: Consul George Logie at Algiers: Swedish letters with 4-digit code words, the plain word written above each group
correspondents: George Logie (Swedish consul at Algiers), and a letter about him probably by his secretary -> the Kanslikollegium / Kanslipresident (Stockholm)
language: Swedish (code: underlined 4-digit groups 1000-1999 inside clear sentences)
shelfmark: Riksarkivet, Diplomatica Turcica, bihang Algerica, SE/RA/2119/2119.2/2/2 (Svenska konsulers skrivelser, Georg Logie, 1729-1739)
folio_note: 526 images (series R0002319), all paged (267-526 again at 600 px). Code at 281-282 (letter signed George Logie, Algiers 24 May 1736; signature on 283) and 300 (letter of June-July 1736, docket No. 162 of 12 July 1736 on 299). Images 2-266 seen only at 300 px, where this form does not show.
status: Catalogue: consul's letters, no mention of cipher. Glossed: every code group carries its plain word written above (2600 px crops of 281, 282, 300): `Signaler 1557.1126.1255.1655.1062`, `Deyen 1233` (in both letters), `Amiralen 1675.1324.1705.1655`, `Algierisk 1443.1657`, `Caparen 1311.1110.1712`, `Turcar 1297`, `Levanten 1259`, `Tractat 1584`, `Sverige 1531`. Words are spelled with several groups (syllables or a small nomenclator). No key in the volume.
why: An early Swedish consular code from the Barbary coast (two years after the 1729 Swedish-Algerian treaty), dated and glossed: key material for any bare Algiers letters of the 1730s.
verify: Collect the group/word pairs from 281, 282, 300; page 2-266 of this volume and Algerica 2/3 (R0002320) at 600 px for more letters in this code, glossed or bare; look for the table in the Kanslikollegium cipher collections.
